analysis.title: GS Contessa - US EQUITIES COLOR Q4 DAY 1 1 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 closed +20bps at 7,666 with a $4.5B market-on-close imbalance to buy. NDX +31bps at 30,501, R2K +37bps at 2,807, Dow +4bps at 50,927. Volume was 17.101bn shares vs YTD daily average of 18.663bn.
Cross-asset closes: VIX +49bps at 16.42, WTI crude +304bps at $93.17, US 10Y yield -5bps at 5.23%, gold +54bps at 4,179, DXY +57bps at 102.03, Bitcoin +135bps at $84,754.

The rates curve continued to bull-steepen after PCE and recent dovish Fed speakers. October hike odds fell to 30%, with about 3 hikes priced through year-end 2027. The rates desk saw a variety of buyers in front-end rates.
France's fiscal consolidation plan drove cross-border moves and a flight to safety. DXY had a roughly 2 standard deviation positive move on the day.

Tech earnings drove squeezes: ACN +16% and an investor day move in SNPS +13% pushed popular shorts and perceived AI-at-risk names higher (GSTMTAIR +3.7%). Most hedge funds wanted to add shorts in this complex on the move, but the desk saw more buying than selling there.
Activity was spotty. The desk's floor activity was a 4 on a 1-10 scale, with client skews benign.

Post-bell, NKE fell 6%. The top line missed and EPS was intact, but the focus was the FY guide, which was a big cut. It came in below most base-case cuts and roughly in line with the worst bear cases. At the midpoint of the new guide the stock trades at 26x P/E. An analyst day is next month.

GS estimates September NFP at +80k vs consensus +88k. Layoffs remain low and big-data job indicators picked up sequentially. September payrolls tend to underperform trend when Labor Day falls late in the month, and last month's jump was boosted by leisure and hospitality and local education hiring that GS does not expect to repeat.

GS estimates the unemployment rate edged down to 4.0% from 4.1% in the prior month, reflecting lower continuing claims. GS forecasts average hourly earnings +0.2% m/m, below consensus, on negative calendar effects.

Derivatives: the morning selloff was led by credit markets, and the desk saw real panic for the first time in weeks. Vol caught a firm bid as spot fell, which the desk called a return of normal spot/vol behavior. Skew and vol of vol were also bid.
Customers added hedges in QQQ and IWM, but flows stayed disconnected from sentiment as chips remain off the table.

SPX fixed-strike vols relaxed as the market recovered and closed essentially unchanged, while front-month skew held its bid. RUT fixed-strike vols were bid in gamma tenors and offered in the back end of the curve.
Single stocks and thematics were a stock picker's market with no particular sector lean.
A large MRVL trade was seen: paper bought 15,000 x 7,500 Jan28 280 ratio straddle flex, about 2.5mln vega.
The desk thinks nuclear names look interesting after the US/South Korea deal, with investors starkly underexposed.
The S&P implied move for tomorrow's payrolls is 67bps.
